chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Jameel, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That which is between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon a channel from the channels of Paradise, and the legs of my pulpit were grown in Paradise.'
He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'Is it a garden today?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, indeed, if the cover were removed, you would see it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the space between the Prophet's house and his pulpit?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the metaphysical reality of the Prophet's pulpit area in Medina, affirming that the 'garden of Paradise' is not merely a future eschatological promise but a present, veiled reality accessible to the faithful. In Shia tradition, this underscores the sanctity of the Prophet's physical presence and the continuity of divine grace in the world, as confirmed by the Imam's affirmation that the veil is simply lifted for those with spiritual insight.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Jameel, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘In what is between my<sup>saww</sup> house and my<sup>saww</sup> Pulpit, there is a Garden from the Gardens of the Paradise, and my<sup>saww</sup> Pulpit is upon a channel from the channels of the Paradise, and the legs of my<sup>saww</sup> Pulpit were grown in the Paradise’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘Is it a Garden today?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, if the cover is removed, you would see it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from, Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Jamil from abu Bakr af-Hadramiy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Between my house and my pulpit there is a garden of the gardens of paradise. My pulpit is on a passageway of the passageways of paradise. The legs of my pulpit had grown in paradise.’
I (the narrator) asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Is it a garden today?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, it is a garden today. If the curtain is removed, you can see it.’”
